Ava (AE): Heads up - Prospect EdgeProxyCorp wants Redwood in their account via PrivateLink. They also insist all outbound traffic egresses via their on-prem security stack and the security team needs original client IPs in our logs. Thoughts?
Jon SE: PrivateLink is fine for control plane and API access. Preserving original 5-tuple at our collectors is hard if traffic is NATed. Quick options: 1) accept X-Forwarded-For from their proxy + mTLS and signed attestations; 2) set up a customer-facing VPN/DirectConnect so packets keep original IPs; 3) route via TGW/VPC peering with host-based forwarding (complicated). For POC, 1 is fastest.
Riley (NetEng): Agree. Technical note: Interface endpoints create ENIs in their subnets; flows originate from those ENI IPs toward our service in AWS. If they do a proxied egress to on-prem, Redwood will see proxy IPs unless they add original source in header. If auditors refuse XFF, only dedicated private connectivity (DX/VPN) works.
Priya (Security): Auditors usually accept header-based provenance if we provide immutable signed logs and mutual authentication. We'll need to validate request signatures server-side and capture header-to-source mapping. Also require HSTS/TLS termination rules documented.
Ava (AE): They asked about cost delta vs public API for POC (hourly interface endpoint + data transfer). Can we give a ballpark?
Jon SE: Interface endpoint costs: hourly per endpoint (~$0.01-$0.02/hr depending on region) + per-GB data processing for cross-AZ. If POC traffic small, hourly cost dominates. For data: estimate egress GBs * region egress pricing (very small for internal AWS). If they NAT out to on-prem, there's additional egress charges on their side. I'll provide conservative numbers.
Riley (NetEng): We should also ask them whether they want failover to our public endpoints. If yes, they must whitelist our public egress IP ranges in their outbound firewall. Fallback policy: prefer privatelink, then public.
Ava (AE): They also submitted the vendor security questionnaire. Priya, any blockers?
Priya (Security): POC-level: okay with header-based source if we lock down mTLS and log signing. Production: request DirectConnect or private interconnect, SOC2 gap must be closed for long-term. I'll attach required attestations list.
Ava (AE): Can someone paste a simple firewall rule they can copy into their change ticket (Cisco ASA style)?
Riley (NetEng): Sure - short snippet:
```
access-list OUTBOUND permit tcp 10.20.0.0 255.255.0.0 host 172.31.5.10 eq 443
access-list OUTBOUND permit udp any host 172.31.5.10 range 1024 65535
object-group service REDWOOD-API tcp eq 443
policy-map type inspect REDWOOD-INSPECT
```
Note: replace 172.31.5.10 with the interface endpoint IPs we'll share. If they use NAT, allow ephemeral ports 1024-65535.
Jon SE: SG sample for the endpoint subnets: allow outbound 443 to our service CIDRs, allow inbound from their app subnets for health checks (TCP 443).
Ava (AE): Action items?
Priya (Security): 1) We accept X-Forwarded-For for POC with mTLS + signed logs; will draft wording.
Jon SE: 2) I'll send estimated endpoint hourly + 50GB egress price delta for the POC.
Riley (NetEng): 3) I'll generate the precise IP list for interface endpoints and confirm failover public IPs.
deploy-bot: Runbook link created: https://redwood.internal/deals/edgeproxycorp/poc-privatelink (auto-created).
Ava (AE): Thanks team. I'll loop in the customer's netsec and schedule a 30m handoff call tomorrow. :calendar:
